name: WWB SEO Master
author: Aleks

sections.description:
SEO made easier

WWB SEO Master is a free WordPress SEO plugin that helps search engines understand
your website and helps you control how your pages can appear in search results and
when shared on social media. You do not need to be an SEO expert: the plugin
explains what it finds, why it matters and what you can do next.

Start with the essentials such as SEO titles and meta descriptions, then use the
technical, structured-data and content tools when you need them. Modules can be
enabled separately, so you stay in control of what runs on your site.

Main features

  • Write SEO titles and meta descriptions for posts, pages and public taxonomies.
  • Set canonical URLs and robots metadata to control preferred URLs and indexing.
  • Add Open Graph and X metadata for clearer social-media sharing.
  • Generate connected JSON-LD structured data with a guided schema builder.
  • Use the WordPress XML sitemap with additional sitemap and robots.txt controls.
  • Run understandable content audits and technical SEO scans with prioritized actions.
  • Find internal-link opportunities and pages that may need more incoming links.
  • Create redirects, automatically redirect changed permalinks and monitor 404 errors.
  • Add breadcrumbs and manage SEO for categories, tags and other public taxonomies.
  • Control indexing and redirects for author archives, date archives and media attachment pages.
  • Import supported metadata from Yoast SEO, Rank Math, SEOPress and All in One SEO.
  • View optional read-only Google Search Console reports and inspect individual URLs.
  • Use multilingual checks and integrations for common WordPress content workflows.

AEO, GEO and AI search tools

Search is changing, but the basics still matter. Clear metadata, crawlable pages,
useful content and accurate structured data help traditional search engines and
can also make content easier for answer engines and AI-powered search to understand.

WWB SEO Master includes answer helpers, entity-based schema, AI crawler controls
and an optional /llms.txt file. These tools support answer engine optimization
(AEO), generative engine optimization (GEO) and AI-search readiness, but they do
not guarantee rankings, citations or inclusion in AI answers. Google Search does
not currently use llms.txt.

The optional AI assistant can suggest metadata and content improvements. AI is
disabled by default, runs only after an authorized user requests it and never
publishes changes automatically. WordPress 7.0 or newer can use the built-in
WordPress AI Client. Older versions can use an administrator-configured OpenAI
fallback.

Privacy and control

There are no advertisements, license checks or usage telemetry. Most features run
entirely on your WordPress site. Optional external services are documented below
and are contacted only when an authorized user configures and uses them.

Deactivation keeps your settings and SEO metadata. When the plugin is deleted,
permanent cleanup follows the setting under WWB SEO > Settings. Clean removal is
enabled by default for new installations; existing installations keep their saved
preference.

External Services

This plugin has no licensing, update-check, advertising, analytics or telemetry
service. The following optional services are used only when a site administrator
configures and invokes their associated features.

WordPress AI Client and configured AI provider

On WordPress 7.0 or newer, the plugin first calls wp_ai_client_prompt(). The
WordPress AI Client selects a compatible AI provider from connectors installed
and configured by the site owner. WWB SEO does not install a connector and does
not control which provider the owner selects.

When an authorized administrator manually requests page optimization, the prompt may
contain the site name, locale, saved page title, saved SEO/social metadata,
schema type and a bounded plain-text copy of the saved page content. When an
administrator manually requests backlink candidates, it may contain the site
name and URL, business goal, audience, location and up to eight recent public
page titles and URLs. That second request also asks a capable provider to use web
search. No prompt is sent automatically or in the background.

Data handling, retention, billing, terms and privacy are determined by the AI
connector and provider configured by the site owner. See the
WordPress AI Client documentation
and the selected connector/provider documentation before enabling this feature.

OpenAI fallback

The optional backward-compatible fallback sends manual AI requests to
https://api.openai.com/v1/responses. It is used only when the WordPress AI
Client is unavailable or cannot support the requested capability and a site
administrator has saved an OpenAI API key.

Page-optimization and backlink-candidate requests contain the same bounded data
described above. A pseudonymous HMAC identifier derived from the current local
user ID can also be sent for abuse prevention; it is not the WordPress username,
email address or raw user ID. Requests set store: false. Backlink research may
enable OpenAI web search. The encrypted API key remains on the WordPress site and
is transmitted only in the authorization header for the request. Nothing is sent
until an authorized user explicitly runs an AI action.

OpenAI API use is subject to OpenAI’s
terms and
privacy policy. API usage may be
billed to the key owner.

Google OAuth and Search Console

The optional Search Console module communicates with these Google endpoints:

  • https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth for administrator-initiated OAuth consent.
  • https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token to exchange and refresh OAuth tokens.
  • https://www.googleapis.com/webmasters/v3/ for verified properties and read-only performance reports.
  • https://searchconsole.googleapis.com/v1/urlInspection/index:inspect for administrator-requested URL inspection.

The OAuth client ID, authorization code, encrypted client secret and encrypted
tokens are used for authentication. Selected property, date ranges, report
dimensions and administrator-entered inspection URLs are sent as needed. The
module requests the read-only webmasters.readonly scope. Performance results
are cached locally for one hour and inspection results for six hours. Disconnect
removes stored tokens and the selected property. Google use is subject to the
Google Terms of Service and
Google Privacy Policy.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin ZIP in Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate WWB SEO Master.
  3. Open WWB SEO > Settings and enable only the modules you need.
  4. Set the public identity used by the schema graph.
  5. Edit content or public taxonomy terms to configure SEO fields.
  6. Back up the site before using migration or permanent uninstall cleanup.
sections.faq:
Is a license key required?

No. There is no license-key system, advertising or telemetry.

Is WordPress 7.0 required?

No. The minimum remains WordPress 6.0. WordPress 7.0 or newer can use the native
AI Client; older versions can use the optional direct OpenAI fallback.

Does AI publish or change content automatically?

No. AI runs only on an authorized manual action. Suggestions must be selected,
reviewed and saved by the user. Backlink candidates also require manual adoption
and outreach.

Does deactivation delete SEO data?

No. Deactivation never deletes data. Optional permanent cleanup applies only
when the plugin itself is deleted and the setting was enabled beforehand. Clean
removal is enabled for new installations; existing installations keep their
previous choice so an update never changes a data-retention preference silently.

Does llms.txt improve Google rankings or AI Overviews?

No. Google states that Search ignores llms.txt. WWB provides it only as an
experimental, optional discovery file for other services that may choose to
read the convention.

Does it replace the WordPress sitemap?

It controls and extends the sitemap system built into WordPress. The sitemap
index remains available at /wp-sitemap.xml.
sections.changelog:
5.7.1

  • Added simple Index, Noindex, and Disable controls for author archives.
  • Removed noindexed or disabled author archives from the WordPress XML sitemap.
  • Added an optional permanent homepage redirect when author archives are disabled.
  • Added Index, Noindex, and Disable controls for date archives.
  • Added options to keep, noindex, or redirect thin media attachment pages.
  • Completed sitemap exclusion scans for sites with more than 500 matching posts or terms.
  • Made migration rollback resumable until every backup has been restored.
  • Restricted use of the site-wide AI provider and quota to administrators by default, with a filterable capability.

5.7.0

  • Rewrote the WordPress.org description in plain language and improved discovery for SEO, metadata, schema, AEO, GEO and AI-search topics.
  • Fixed migration detection and explained supported fields, zero results and unchanged imports.
  • Prevented unresolved title-template variables from being copied as literal page metadata.
  • Added clear indexability explanations and direct links to each page’s SEO panel.
  • Made title length, content depth and link suggestions optional guidance outside the core score.
  • Removed rigid 60/160-character storage limits while retaining practical display guidance.
  • Replaced harsh audit wording with Needs attention, Review and Optional statuses.
  • Made technical scans continue automatically and grouped results by type and affected pages.
  • Listed missing schema fields, added direct edit links and reduced false Article schema findings.
  • Completed uninstall cleanup for legacy WWB option keys and enabled clean removal by default for new installations.
  • Clarified that llms.txt is experimental and is ignored by Google Search.

Earlier release notes are available in changelog.txt inside the plugin package.
